missing_evidence: No complete warm plans or historical optimizer iterations: capabilities list update:30:complete_warm_and_plans and update:34:complete_warm_and_plans as missing, so stopping quality (relative_seed_improvement at iteration 16 versus Solve_Succeeded at iteration 31) cannot be reconstructed.

No full backend state: full_snapshots_available is false and snapshot_id is null for the retained updates, so only the recorded projected-state difference (curvature_linf_rad_m 0.3593342665423016, rate_linf_rad_m_s 11.650736824112833 at update 30) is available and no complete-state agreement can be assessed.

No simulated-time timing/staleness records: no artifact reports when a controller command was consumed relative to integration steps, so any delay mechanism from the wall-clock misses is unrecorded and unsupported.

No counterfactual evidence: no trajectory, plan or comparison exists under a non-zero tip-speed weight, a different horizon, or a longer sampling duration, so the zero-penalty and horizon-truncation hypotheses cannot be settled from retained evidence alone.
No post-horizon trail: the evidence ends at t = 0.35 s, so whether the 0.635 m/s terminal speed would decay below 0.02 m/s shortly afterwards is untested.
No model-fidelity evidence beyond one step: aligned comparisons cover a single interval each and are explicitly scoped away from full state agreement.

recommendations.rationale: The retained evidence fixes the failing criterion (residual terminal tip speed inside the settling window) and the deadline-miss timing profile, but cannot separate a braking/terminal-speed deficit from horizon truncation or from a merely weak speed penalty; a controller-parameter change now would be an unsupported guess, so defer until the single bounded saved-state check described in the report is executed and its selectors cited.

Provisional only and inside the protocol bounds [0.0001, 1.0]: the recorded recipe keeps holding_tip_speed_weight at 0.0 while the tip still moves at 0.635 m/s at the end of the horizon, so the smallest allowed non-zero braking penalty is the bounded candidate the check should compare against. Support is currently weak (no counterfactual run) and adoption of this exact value requires a separate matched design adoption.

attribution.reason: Terminal position error is inside the 0.01 m limit while every sampled speed in the final 0.05 s window (0.861872864376846, 1.32948286853263, 1.4769184551353305, 1.5810152739742807, 0.7758084264853817, 0.6351726092425104 m/s) exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, so the failed criterion is the speed criterion, observed as motion that has not decayed by the end of the sampling horizon. This is a statement about the recorded trajectory only; it does not identify why the residual speed persists.

Retained per-update wall time exceeds the 0.01 s control period in every update, with optimization_solve_s and warm_preparation_s accounting for most of it (8.591 s of 8.591 s and 3.232 s of 3.453 s in the two retained updates), plus 34 of 35 updates ending in User_Requested_Stop.

No retained artifact records a simulated-time consequence of the misses: no command-staleness, queue or delay field is present, snapshot_id is null and full_snapshots_available is false, and the supplied scheduling semantics state that commands complete synchronously before fixed-count integration steps and that wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time. The retained evidence cannot connect the misses to the residual tip speed without an unrecorded delay mechanism.

holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 coincide with a tip still moving at 0.635 m/s at the end of the horizon, so a weak braking/terminal-velocity penalty is consistent with the observation; no retained artifact contains a counterfactual trajectory under a different weight, so this stays a candidate for the bounded check rather than an established cause.

One-step aligned comparisons bound prediction agreement (input applied exactly, velocity differences 0.15 and 0.019 m/s, tip differences ~6 mm and ~1 mm) and explicitly exclude full backend-state agreement, so they neither confirm nor exclude a systematic speed under-prediction across the several steps of the settling window.

Speed declines from its 1.5810152739742807 m/s peak to 0.6351726092425104 m/s within the last 0.03 s of the 0.35 s window, but the retained evidence contains no post-horizon extrapolation or longer-horizon trail, so whether the tip would satisfy the 0.02 m/s limit later in simulated time is untested.

facts.statement: In the retained baseline summary, reach_passed = true and sampled_settling_passed = false are distinct outcomes of the same run: terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m lies inside the 0.01 m reach/settling position limit, while terminal_speed_m_s = 0.6351726092425104 m/s and late_max_speed_m_s = 1.5810152739742807 m/s far exceed the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit; the same summary reports deadline_misses = 35 against control_period_s = 0.01 s. Reach, sampled settling and real-time feasibility are therefore recorded as separate result fields, not as one conflated pass/fail.

The late-motion samples show monotone position-error decay (0.05813810428573256, 0.04778599698437965, 0.03407510504995951, 0.019054532266831993, 0.0100658278018921, 0.007642608585867386 m at t = 0.30 to 0.35 s) while tip speed peaks at 1.5810152739742807 m/s at t = 0.33 s and is still 0.6351726092425104 m/s at the final sampled time t = 0.35 s; every sample inside the 0.05 s settling window at the end of the horizon has speed above the 0.02 m/s limit.

For the two retained non-initialization updates, update_wall_s = 8.590574299916625 s (update_id 30) and 3.4527177999261767 s (update_id 34) against a 0.01 s control period, dominated by optimization_solve_s = 6.753986699972302 s / 2.885958099970594 s and warm_preparation_s = 1.6389210999477655 s / 0.34554179990664124 s; the summary reports mean_update_s = 17.075238151415917 s, 35 deadline misses and stopping counts Solve_Succeeded = 1 versus User_Requested_Stop = 34 (update_id 30 policy_stop_reason = relative_seed_improvement; update_id 34 optimization_raw_status = Solve_Succeeded, policy_stop_reason = null).

The aligned one-step comparisons show the recorded input was applied unchanged (applied_input_difference_n = 0.0) with tip_difference_m = 0.006240614340723002 m / 0.001183439178222365 m and velocity vector_difference_norm_m_s = 0.1534294782532689 / 0.018534244890083693, and the projected-state comparison is explicitly scoped as 'recorded projected states, not full backend-state error'; the controller recipe in the same run has holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02.

gates.reason: terminal_error_m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance.
late_max_speed_m_s and terminal_speed_m_s both exceed the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit inside the 0.05 s window.
mean_update_s exceeds the 0.01 s control period and the summary records 35 deadline misses.

limitations: Read-only review of retained evidence; no solver, backend execution or trajectory evaluation was performed in this phase.
Capabilities reported by the observations file mark update:30 and update:34 complete_warm_and_plans as missing, so no warm plans or historical optimizer iterations were available.
full_snapshots_available is false and snapshot_id is null for both retained updates, so no full projected backend state is bound.
Aligned one-step comparisons are explicitly scoped as projected-state versus serial-backend endpoint at one step only; they do not establish multi-step or full-state agreement.
Single execution; no counterfactual runs, no matched design comparison and no post-horizon trail exist in the retained evidence, so no dominant cause is established.
recommended_actions: Defer any production controller change until one bounded saved-state check resolves whether the end-of-horizon residual tip speed is a braking/terminal-speed modelling deficit or simply the 0.35 s sampling horizon ending before momentum decays; the check must run only on the identified execution's saved projected state or a temporary analysis configuration and must never modify the successful baseline.

Candidate single bounded check (not requested in this report): starting from the saved state for the last update (source_selectors.state_pointer_template /34/measured_initial_state and input /34/actual_tension_n in the state file b59be99a8308a48d4b44c69af4296d51c3b13241679c4b7a6c22ee601d69f770), evaluate model.gvs@1.0.0 with implicit_euler, integration_step_s 0.002 and horizon_s 0.01 under operations prediction_braking and local_comparison, comparing the predicted near-term tip velocity/position against the recorded next-timestamp tip velocity (0.1110353673178959, -0.15545431325459183, -0.6057634416396074 m/s, |v| = 0.6351726092425104 m/s) and tip position of update_id 34; a systematic speed deficit would support the projection-deficit hypothesis, while close agreement would leave the horizon-truncation and zero-speed-penalty hypotheses standing.

Keep reach, sampled settling and real-time feasibility as three separate findings in all downstream text: the deadline misses are a real-time-feasibility result and must not be restated as the cause of the settling deficit without a recorded simulated-time delay mechanism.

Any control-parameter suggestion must stay inside the declared protocol bounds (holding_tip_speed_weight and terminal_tip_speed_weight in [0.0001, 1.0]) and is provisional: adoption of an exact parameter/value would require a separate matched design adoption.
